chosen.premise: At its next evolution, Poliwhirl must choose between a Water Stone or a Kings Rock trade to become different Pokémon.
chosen.hook: Poliwhirl’s evolution splits into two completely different choices.
chosen.visualIdea: Place a Water Stone and Kings Rock trade on opposite sides, branching Poliwhirl into Poliwrath or Politoed.
chosen.note: The branching evolution and contrasting requirements are highly specific and visually clear. It is slightly less surprising to experienced fans, and the evolution methods rely on trusted secondary research.

candidates.premise: Poliwhirl marches onto land for bug Pokémon, then drags them underwater to eat safely.
candidates.hook: Poliwhirl hunts on land—but eats its prey underwater.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate a numbered route: land march, bug capture, underwater retreat, then the full hunting loop.
candidates.note: A concrete, strange hunting routine: Poliwhirl goes onto land for prey, then eats it underwater for safety. The full sequence is explicitly supported and naturally storyboardable.

candidates.premise: Poliwhirl’s undulating belly spiral causes drowsiness and has been used instead of lullabies to put children to sleep.
candidates.hook: Poliwhirl’s belly is basically a living lullaby.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom into the animated belly spiral, overlay growing sleep symbols, then reveal its lullaby use.
candidates.note: The animated spiral and lullaby use create an excellent visual reveal. It is highly supported, but the sleep-inducing spiral is already one of Poliwhirl’s better-known traits.

candidates.premise: Poliwhirl survives capture by sweating slimy mucus that lets it slither out of an enemy’s grasp.
candidates.hook: The Pokémon that escapes by sweating is Poliwhirl.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a hand grabbing Poliwhirl, then its slick body sliding free as mucus coats its skin.
candidates.note: A distinctive escape mechanism, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries. The premise is strong, though the visual of a generic grab-and-slip escape is somewhat familiar.

candidates.premise: When Poliwhirl’s skin dries out, its health suffers, so it must be moisturized diligently.
candidates.hook: For Poliwhirl, dry skin is a genuine health problem.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Poliwhirl’s wet skin fading dry and cracked, then restore its slick coating with water and moisture.
candidates.note: The health consequence of drying out is well supported, but cracked skin and a restorative moisturizing sequence are visual embellishments not stated in the research.

candidates.premise: Poliwhirl can live on land, but it prefers water because it has fewer natural enemies there.
candidates.hook: Poliwhirl can live on land—but treats water like a fortress.
candidates.visualIdea: Split the screen between dangerous land and safer water as Poliwhirl repeatedly retreats underwater.
candidates.note: Accurate and easy to stage, but it is a broad habitat preference rather than a sharply unusual Poliwhirl-specific behavior.
